findings.text: with config_for absent — the only way the admit CLI reaches this pass (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:6663 calls admit_until_stopped(lane=..., once=...) and :6661 admit_once(lane=..., run_id=...); neither passes config_for) — resolve_config is _default_config, declared at :56 as (project, root) and called here with the project alone. The TypeError is swallowed at :133-134, so every mounted project reports 'config: _default_config() missing 1 required positional argument: root' and the service files no request at all. Reproduced by importing this revision's queueing.py and calling PlanQueue().fill(projects=...) with no config_for: {"projects": [{"project": "proj", "plans": [], "error": "config: _default_config() missing 1 required positional argument: 'root'"}], "queued": 0, "filed": []}. Pass root at the call, and add a test that drives fill or admit_once with no config_for.

release_plan is handed _plan_hold_target(run_id, project) with the plan argument omitted (hold at :1113 does the same), so the plan-only branch at :1152 is unreachable and `crew queue hold --plan X` with no --project raises the error whose text offers that branch ('or a plan name registered in mounts.json'); the feature works when --project is named, but the documented fallback cannot run.
the comment line "section's refs moves to ``queued`` the moment the last ref lands and" appears at :141 and again at :142, leaving the paragraph garbled in a file this node edited.

assert hold["plan"]["plan"] == PLAN (and the same shape at :236 for release) compares the record the test's own plan argument produced against that same argument, so it holds whatever the stored hold says; the pass assertions at :232 and :238 are the independent guard, and this one should be dropped or compared against the stored hold file instead.

mounted_projects re-implements the project-to-docs resolution the repository owns at reckon/serve.py:1156 (mounts_for_snapshot, memoised) and reckon/capabilities.py:37 (_mounted_docs), so mounts.json now has a third reader with a third filtering rule.

the timing clause cannot fail: the off arm returns before doing anything and nine of the ten on-arm passes are short-circuited by the identity cache here, so both medians are 0.000 s whatever the stage costs. The one pass that parses plans cost 41.823 s (queue-pass-timing.log), twenty times the two-second bound the clause exists to enforce, and the median hides it. Measure the uncached pass, or state the clause as a first-pass bound.
